en.title: Does a tumor-kinetic model add anything to a single early tumor change?
en.summary: At 16, 24 and 32 weeks, a mixed-effects tumor-kinetic estimate added no held-out survival discrimination beyond the observed one-point change, and carrying the last value forward predicted the next measurement best.
key_findings: At 16, 24 and 32 weeks, a mixed-effects tumor-kinetic estimate changed held-out survival C-index by only +0.002 to +0.016 over the observed one-point change, and every interval included zero.
For the next tumor measurement, carrying the last value forward was the most accurate rule at every landmark (MAE 0.42–0.61), beating both linear and quadratic mixed models.
Kinetic terms correlated about 0.97 with the one-point change, so with this measurement density a simple change suffices; this is not an evaluation of mechanistic TGI models in general.
